X.note: The rock is a decent hero shape, but the foreground is a huge empty green field with a few bare wall segments, thin trench lines and one tiny block of troops. There are no ships, almost no smoke and no sense of a besieging army. The town is a speck on the far right. It reads as an empty landscape, not a siege.

Y.note: Many troop blocks, siege lines, flags, drifting smoke, water and a visible town and church tower. The rock is more dramatic and the composition has depth. The troop blocks look like tiled brown crates or cork boards, not men, so scale is odd. The blocks are scattered with no clear order and the foreground is a bit repetitive. Even so, it reads as a besieging army in front of the rock.

why: Y actually shows an army and siege works on the isthmus with the town visible, while X is mostly empty grass and sky.
top_fix_for_weaker: Fill the foreground with units: add massed infantry, gun batteries with muzzle smoke, tents and men working on the trenches. Add ships off the rock, and move the camera lower and closer so the lines lead the eye to the town.
top_fix_for_better: Replace the crate-like troop blocks with readable soldier figures in lines or columns with varied colours. Add gun emplacements with visible fire and smoke, and organise the blocks into clear approach lines toward the fortress. Add ships on the water and make the town more visible.
